data.title: Ethambutol (E)
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Ethylenediamine derivative; first-line antituberculous drug
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Ethylenediamine derivative; first-line antituberculous drug

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits arabinosyl transferase → blocks arabinogalactan synthesis in the mycobacterial cell wall (bacteriostatic)
- Mainly prevents resistance to other drugs

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- TB (intensive and continuation phases in India's daily regimen), cutaneous TB
- Atypical mycobacteria (M. marinum with clarithromycin; MAC)

## Dose & formulations
- 15 mg/kg/day (range 15–25) in fixed-dose combinations
- Reduce dose/interval in renal impairment

## Adverse effects
- Optic (retrobulbar) neuritis: reduced visual acuity and red–green colour blindness (dose-related, usually reversible if stopped early)
- Hyperuricaemia, peripheral neuropathy, rash (rare)

## Contraindications
- Pre-existing optic neuritis; young children who cannot report visual symptoms (relative)

## Drug interactions
- Aluminium antacids reduce absorption

## Monitoring
- Visual acuity and colour vision (Ishihara) at baseline and monthly

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Optic neuritis — red–green colour vision test
- Used with clarithromycin for M. marinum

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7; Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
